heroHeadline: Month-Long Lull Ends: US Strikes Iran's Larak Island, IRGC Hits Jordan and UAE, Claims Downing a US Drone
heroSubtitle: Day 185 (August 31, 2026): The six-month standoff over dueling Hormuz claims gave way to the first direct US-Iran strike exchange since late July. On Aug 30 (Day 184), US forces struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island that were preparing to fire sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz; CENTCOM spokesman Cdr. Tim Hawkins called it 'limited, precise action,' while the IRGC reported 'several' fighters and civilians killed or wounded without a precise toll. Within hours, the IRGC launched 'Punishment of the Aggressor' — a combined missile-and-drone operation against Jordan's King Hussein and Al Azraq air bases — but Jordan's Armed Forces intercepted all 8 missiles with no damage or casualties. Early Aug 31, Iran's army claimed a drone strike on the UAE's Al Minhad Air Base near Dubai; the UAE confirmed only intercepting a drone over its territorial waters, denied any successful attack, and called it a 'dangerous escalation.' President Trump called Iran's decision to hit multiple Gulf states 'a very good thing' for costing Tehran regional support. The IRGC separately claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone east of the strait around 05:30 on Aug 31 using a domestic air-defense system — unconfirmed by US officials. Brent crude jumped 2.5% to above $90/bbl, reversing weeks of de-escalation pricing tied to the still-unrealized Iran-Oman Hormuz navigation-corridor talks.
